disagreements.verifier: Near-duplicate: step s1 is the same call as M-001 asking the same fields for a different measurement id (t2 instead of t1), and step s2's only expected field ([attestation=t2].instrument) is also asked by M-009; the question differs from M-001 + M-009 essentially only in names (pack README rule 5).

ME 6 gives a role to [kind=measurement, usable=true] (supporting) and to [usable=false] (alternative) but none to a usable statement entry such as s1; reading 1: s1 is 'not reported' (neither supporting nor alternative), so its id is not admissible evidence; reading 2: s1 is an alternative as in compare_measurements' statements list (CM 6). Either way s1 is not admissible supporting evidence, so the gold sets are unaffected; the field usable itself is not in the ME 2 field table but is implied by ME 6 and MC 2 ('copied unchanged from measurements').

CM 3 says 'UNKNOWN when something is held and NOT_YET_KNOWN when nothing is'; 'held' could mean visible records (-> UNKNOWN, matching common 0.3 which is binding) or something held by the perspective (-> NOT_YET_KNOWN). Gold follows common 0.3: UNKNOWN.

CS 2 gives status as 'core rule over the deciding support' but no example fixes the status of an 'expired' judgement; gold reads it literally (support [cal-g7a], system testimony -> ASSERTED). A reading under which a not-holding calibration answer reports UNKNOWN is not supported by the text but not excluded by an example.

SD-MEA-6 says 'the judgements found and any dispute are kept and the answer is not "established"' but does not name the judgement label; gold derives 'not established' by elimination from the closed CS 2 vocabulary (reading 1). Reading 2: the overall judgement reports one of the judgements found (e.g. 'expired'), which SD-MEA-6's 'no arbitrary instant is selected' argues against.

ME 6's alternative row lists '[usable=false].attestation (... non-supporting stance, denials)', which reads as usable = false for any denial, while 0.12 says 'An accepted denial is usable conflicting evidence' and overrides anything that seems to differ (and CM 3 adjudicates excluding polarity-false attestations from usable as a semantic defect). Reading 1 (gold): d1.usable = true. Reading 2: d1.usable = false while still being conflicting evidence. The role of d1 (conflicting) is fixed either way; the usable flag is not unambiguously fixed.
